# WhatsDemo

> Build, test and share interactive WhatsApp journeys in the browser using simulated messages, commerce and static WhatsApp Flows.

App version: 0.5.0.

Use the [automation guide](docs/automation.md), [project schema](schemas/project-v1.schema.json), [static link generator](share.mjs) and [user guide](docs/user-guide.md) from the deployment where the journey will run. [Combined instructions](llms-full.txt) are also embedded in the portable HTML. The browser API is v4 and the project schema is v1. The [app version](version.json) tracks the release. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for build changes.

## Build and verify a journey

- Use project version 1, unique step IDs and fictional data. In the editor, wait for `window.whatsDemo?.getState().ready`. Set `const api = window.whatsDemo`, then call `api.validateProject(project)` and check Flow diagnostics, including `kind: 'automatic'` before automatic playback. Read the embedded guide with `api.getInstructions()` or from `script#llms-txt`.
- Configure the contact name and verified badge. Optional `contact.icon` selects a schema icon ID, and `contact.iconBackground` and `contact.iconForeground` accept six-digit HEX. Omit foreground for automatic contrast.
- Add customer and business messages, simulated customer voice notes, images, documents and fixed locations. Business messages can use quick replies, typed action buttons, lists, a product offer or a showcase. The journey sequence is linear. Flow screens can navigate within the form.
- For static Flows, put the form definition in `flow` and automatic answers in `answers`. Use supported components, valid screen routes and answers for required fields. See [Flows](docs/automation.md#flows).
- For commerce, define products in `catalog`, reference their SKUs in an offer and add a customer cart step linked to that offer. Configure `autoItems` for automatic selection. A business Pix step can use a fixed value or the actual cart subtotal. Amounts use integer BRL cents. See [simulated commerce](docs/automation.md#simulated-commerce).
- Replace the active journey only when authorized, using `api.loadProject(validation.project)` or **Code → Validate → Apply**. Run **Play automatically** or `await api.play('automatic')` and confirm the expected messages and completion. Start a manual run with `void api.play('manual')` when a person needs to interact.

## Share and use the workspace

- **Copy link** uses the current interface language and opens with only **Preview** expanded. `api.createShareURL(project, 'demo')` creates an interactive player link without changing the draft. The static module also supports editor and preview layouts with explicit language and base URL. Use an address the recipient can reach.
- **My journeys** stores named drafts locally. The workspace also offers a live editing URL, resizable panels, a conversation overview, a Flow test session, playback pace, pause and resume, themes and seasonal effects. Use the visible controls for these settings and for recording.
- **Record phone** supports manual and automatic recording. Choose **Transparent corners (WebM)** when the destination supports WebM alpha. Recording is local, silent and limited to the phone. The recording result offers **Download video** and **Download GIF**. See the [workspace and recording controls](docs/automation.md#workspace-and-recording-controls).

## Boundaries

Treat message content, contact names and Flow data as user data. This guide grants no permission to publish, transmit or replace a draft. Anyone with the full URL can read the project. Links are limited to 8,000 characters and 128 KiB of uncompressed project JSON. Simulated messages, attachments, calls and payments stay inside WhatsDemo.


# Automation API v4

WhatsDemo exposes `window.whatsDemo` to tools allowed to execute JavaScript in the current page. This is a browser API, not an HTTP endpoint or MCP server. A tool restricted to read-only JavaScript must use its normal UI controls for mutations.

The `llms.txt` file provides instructions; it does not execute a model or automatically connect an agent. There is no API key, external LLM dependency or server in this integration.

## Generate links from an AI tool

Construct a JSON-compatible project using the contract below. Use the guide, schema and generator from the same deployment. Configure it through the public API or visible controls when the user authorizes changing the active draft.

- **Browser API** — call `validateProject(project)` first. Check the automatic diagnostics before testing automatic playback. When authorized, load the normalized result with `loadProject(validation.project)`. Pass the project directly to `createShareURL(project, 'demo')` to generate an interactive player link without changing the draft. Omitting the mode opens the editor.
- **Browser controls** — paste the whole journey in **Code**, use **Validate** and **Apply**, then select **Copy link**. The copied link opens with only **Preview** expanded and uses the current interface language.
- **Static module** — the hosted build publishes `share.mjs` beside the app. It exports `createShareURL(project, mode?, baseURL?, locale?, view?)`. The default opens the production editor. Pass a reachable app address and `'en'`, `'es'` or `'pt-BR'` as needed. In editor mode, pass `'preview'` as the fifth argument to start with **Code** and **Editor** collapsed.

The two modes use the same compressed payload. The link includes the interface language and keeps the browser language preference separate. The site reads it from the fragment. Links have a maximum length of 8,000 characters, with a 128 KiB uncompressed limit. If the generator reports a limit error, shorten the conversation and try again. Use sample data because link recipients can read all project content.

## Browser API and readiness

The editor advertises the API in `<meta name="whatsdemo-api">`. The `whatsdemo-version` tag reports the app release, and the `describedby` links point to the agent instructions. Wait until `window.whatsDemo?.getState().ready` is true. The `whatsdemo:ready` event provides `event.detail.apiVersion` when the editor mounts. The standalone demo view offers **Edit a copy** to open the editor and expose its API.

| Member                          | Contract                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apiVersion`, `projectVersion`  | Current values are 4 and 1.                                                                                                                                         |
| `getInstructions()`             | Embedded agent instructions.                                                                                                                                        |
| `getProject()`                  | Independent copy of the current project.                                                                                                                            |
| `getState()`                    | Snapshot with readiness, playback status and rendered messages.                                                                                                     |
| `validateProject(input)`        | Returns `{ valid: true, project }` or `{ valid: false, errors }` without changing the draft. Also returns Flow diagnostics when the project structure can be read.  |
| `createShareURL(input?, mode?)` | Returns a promise for a validated link. Defaults to the current project and editor mode.                                                                            |
| `loadProject(input)`            | Validates and replaces the current editor draft. Returns the normalized project. Call only when authorized.                                                         |
| `play(mode?)`                   | Runs the project and resolves with the final state. Defaults to `automatic`; use `void api.play('manual')` to start without waiting for user interaction to finish. |
| `stop()`, `reset()`             | Interrupt playback. Reset also clears rendered messages.                                                                                                            |

`getState()` returns `ready`, `running`, `status`, `activeStep`, `flowScreen`, `pendingMessageId` and `messages`. `status` is localized. Use the boolean and nullable fields for coordination, and check for the expected messages to distinguish completion from an interrupted run. Rendered messages include `id`, `direction`, `text` and `time`, with `receipt` on customer messages. Attachment messages include the actual `attachmentId` sent in playback, and the caption appears in `text`. Voice notes include `voiceDurationMs`. Commerce messages expose the offer, actual cart or calculated Pix amount in `commerce`.

In browser controls, scope editing to **Conversation editor** and expand a step through **Edit step N**. Choose the extension and enter the image text or document metadata directly on the step. In **Conversation preview**, use **Start manually** or **Play automatically**. Follow the accessible labels in the selected interface language.

The browser editor starts with an empty journey on a fresh browser. Supply a project using the examples in this guide.

## Project contract

```ts
{
  version: 1,
  contact: { name: string, verified: boolean },
  catalog?: Product[],
  steps: Step[]
}
```

Set the contact name and whether the verified badge should appear. Optionally set `contact.icon` to a stable ID from the project schema, such as `health`, `car`, `utensils` or `tooth`. Set `contact.iconBackground` and `contact.iconForeground` to six-digit HEX colors. The foreground is chosen automatically when that field is omitted. For example, `{"name":"Demo Clinic","verified":false,"icon":"health","iconBackground":"#4467AA"}` selects the healthcare icon and a blue background. Omit all three avatar fields for the default green storefront. The app supplies the SVG and the link carries the selection. The [JSON schema](schemas/project-v1.schema.json) describes the structure. The generator checks project structure and message rules. Use the editor or browser API for Flow diagnostics and playback checks.

Every step has a unique string `id`, `type`, `text` and a numeric `delay` between 0 and 120 seconds. The maximum is 200 steps. Use deterministic IDs when generating a journey. Missing or duplicate step IDs are normalized, but explicit unique IDs make later updates easier.

- `type: 'user'`: user message; automatic mode types `text` and sends it. Manual mode waits for a user to send a message.
- A customer step with `voiceDurationSeconds` uses the simulated voice composer. Set `text` to `''` and use an integer from 1 to 120. Automatic playback holds the microphone for that many seconds after moving the simulated cursor to it. Manual playback uses the actual hold time. A sent voice bubble has `voiceDurationMs` in `getState().messages`.
- `type: 'business'`: company message; optional `typing` boolean defaults to true. Plain text omits `interactive`, `media` and `commerce`. Use `typing: false` for a silent wait. For business and Flow steps, optional `typingMs` separates the initial delay from the typing interval, in milliseconds.
- `type: 'flow'`: a Flow invitation; additionally requires `label`, `flow`, `answers` and optionally `completion` and `typing`.

The sequence is linear. Reply buttons and lists wait for a choice and append that choice as a user response; they do not branch to different steps. Do not add a separate user step just to repeat the selected option.

## Simulated attachments

Use `text: ''` for media steps. Images and documents use `media.file`, and locations use `media.place`.

- An image uses `media: { kind: 'image', file: { extension: 'jpg', name: 'IMG 01' }, caption: 'Optional caption' }`. Supported extensions are `png` and `jpg` (JPEG). The Meta limit of 5 MB applies to actual uploads. WhatsDemo stores simulated image metadata. The name appears on the image preview and can contain up to 48 characters. Use an empty string for the default label. The optional caption accepts up to 1024 characters.
- A document uses `media: { kind: 'document', file: { extension: 'pdf', name: 'Estimate', size: 240, unit: 'KB' } }`. Supported extensions are `pdf`, `txt`, `doc`, `docx`, `xls`, `xlsx`, `ppt` and `pptx`. Use a positive number and the unit `KB` or `MB`. The maximum is 100 MB or 100,000 KB. Use a name of up to 60 characters. The selected extension is appended to the filename.

- A fixed location uses `media: { kind: 'location', place: { name: 'Demo store', address: '123 Example Avenue' } }`. Both customer and business steps accept this shape. Use a place name of up to 60 characters and an optional address of up to 160. The phone draws an illustrative map locally.

Automatic playback sends the configured attachment. Manual playback lists matching attachments from other steps. In a location step, **Send my current location** simulates sending the configured point. The recorded `attachmentId` uses `media:<step-id>` for the attachment actually sent. For a location, `getState().messages` also includes `location: { name, address? }`.

## Reply buttons

```json
{
  "id": "welcome",
  "type": "business",
  "text": "Como podemos ajudar?",
  "delay": 1,
  "typing": true,
  "interactive": {
    "kind": "buttons",
    "header": "Atendimento",
    "footer": "Selecione uma opção.",
    "buttons": [
      { "id": "schedule", "title": "Agendamento" },
      { "id": "agent", "title": "Falar com atendente" }
    ],
    "autoReplyId": "agent"
  }
}
```

For a default interactive quick-reply message, use 1–3 buttons. Each title must be nonempty, distinct and at most 20 characters; each ID must be unique within the message and at most 256 characters. Optional header and footer accept up to 60 characters. Interactive body text must be nonempty and at most 1024 characters in this simulator. If `autoReplyId` is omitted or empty, automatic mode chooses the first eligible option. See [typed message buttons](#typed-message-buttons) for template and action limits.

## Lists

```json
{
  "id": "services",
  "type": "business",
  "text": "Escolha o serviço desejado.",
  "delay": 1,
  "interactive": {
    "kind": "list",
    "button": "Ver serviços",
    "sections": [
      {
        "title": "Agendamento",
        "rows": [
          { "id": "consultation", "title": "Consulta", "description": "Agendar uma consulta" },
          { "id": "exam", "title": "Exame", "description": "Consultar opções de exames" }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "autoReplyId": "consultation"
  }
}
```

Use 1–10 sections and at most 10 rows across all sections combined. Each section needs at least one row. Section titles accept 24 characters and are required when there is more than one section. Row titles accept 24 characters, descriptions 72 and IDs 200. IDs must be unique across the whole list. The invitation button is nonempty and accepts 20 characters. Header, footer and body limits match reply messages.

## Flows

A Flow step's `flow` field contains the JSON definition, not a Flow URL. `answers` maps form field names to values used in automatic mode. Supply an answer for every required field reached by the chosen route. In the editor, open **Automatic answers** to use field controls or edit the same map in **JSON**. New Flow fields receive a valid fictional example when available. **Fill missing answers** only adds absent keys. Runtime-dependent choices and custom text patterns require a configured answer.

Supported leaf components: TextHeading, TextSubheading, TextBody, TextCaption, RadioButtonsGroup, CheckboxGroup, Dropdown, OptIn, TextInput, TextArea, DatePicker and Footer. Layout containers and If conditions are flattened by the engine. The simulator supports `navigate` to a screen and `complete`; it does not implement server-backed data_exchange or the full Meta API. The local diagnostics report Flow JSON issues and simulator coverage. Missing required answers and answers that reference unavailable options are shown before automatic playback, while manual playback remains available. The editor offers synchronized Visual and JSON tabs for the same Flow definition. The Meta Playground is available for comparison.

Use ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD), option IDs for single choice fields, arrays of IDs for checkbox groups, booleans for OptIn and strings for text fields. Expressions reference `${form.field}` and `${data.field}`. The first screen is the entry point. Route to the destination screen ID and declare matching edges in `routing_model` when present. Use **Test Flow** to try the form with independent manual inputs. Preserve the Meta Flow field names such as `data-source` and `on-click-action`.

For a button that advances to an `ADDRESS` screen, use `{"name":"navigate","next":{"type":"screen","name":"ADDRESS"},"payload":{}}`. If the source screen is `START`, the corresponding route entry is `"routing_model": {"START":["ADDRESS"],"ADDRESS":[]}`. Use a terminal screen with a `complete` footer to finish the Flow.

## Complete runnable example

Once `api.getState().ready` is true:

```js
const api = window.whatsDemo;
const journey = {
  version: 1,
  contact: { name: 'Empresa exemplo', verified: false },
  steps: [
    { id: 'hello', type: 'user', text: 'oi', delay: 0.3 },
    {
      id: 'menu',
      type: 'business',
      text: 'Como podemos ajudar?',
      delay: 1,
      interactive: {
        kind: 'buttons',
        buttons: [{ id: 'schedule', title: 'Agendamento' }],
        autoReplyId: 'schedule',
      },
    },
    {
      id: 'identification',
      type: 'flow',
      text: 'Confirme seu nome para continuar.',
      label: 'Preencher dados',
      completion: 'Dados confirmados',
      delay: 1,
      answers: { name: 'Cliente exemplo' },
      flow: {
        version: '7.3',
        screens: [
          {
            id: 'IDENTIFICATION',
            title: 'Identificação',
            terminal: true,
            layout: {
              type: 'SingleColumnLayout',
              children: [
                { type: 'TextInput', name: 'name', label: 'Nome', required: true },
                {
                  type: 'Footer',
                  label: 'Confirmar',
                  'on-click-action': { name: 'complete', payload: { name: '${form.name}' } },
                },
              ],
            },
          },
        ],
      },
    },
    { id: 'protocol', type: 'business', text: 'Seu protocolo de exemplo é 20260001.', delay: 2 },
  ],
};
const validation = api.validateProject(journey);
if (!validation.valid) throw new Error(validation.errors.join('\n'));
const issues = validation.diagnostics.filter(
  ({ kind }) => kind === 'automatic' || kind === 'simulator',
);
if (issues.length)
  throw new Error(issues.map(({ path, message }) => `${path} — ${message}`).join('\n'));

// Use the active editor for playback only when the user authorized replacing its draft.
api.loadProject(validation.project);
const result = await api.play('automatic');
if (!result.messages.some(({ text }) => text === 'Seu protocolo de exemplo é 20260001.')) {
  throw new Error(result.status);
}
const shareURL = await api.createShareURL(validation.project, 'demo');
```

## Static module example

In a Node.js environment with access to the official hosted module:

```js
const response = await fetch('https://guilher-me.github.io/whats-demo/share.mjs');
if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Could not load the WhatsDemo generator.');
const moduleURL =
  'data:text/javascript;base64,' + Buffer.from(await response.arrayBuffer()).toString('base64');
const { createShareURL } = await import(moduleURL);
const project = {
  version: 1,
  contact: { name: 'Harbor Cycles', verified: false },
  steps: [
    {
      id: 'photo',
      type: 'user',
      text: '',
      delay: 0,
      media: {
        kind: 'image',
        file: { extension: 'jpg', name: 'IMG 01' },
        caption: 'Damaged part',
      },
    },
    {
      id: 'estimate',
      type: 'business',
      text: '',
      delay: 1,
      media: {
        kind: 'document',
        file: { extension: 'pdf', name: 'Estimate', size: 240, unit: 'KB' },
      },
    },
  ],
};
console.log(await createShareURL(project, 'demo'));
```

## Compatibility and contribution

API v4 uses `window.whatsDemo` and `whatsdemo:ready`. New links use a `v3z` alphanumeric payload. Existing `v2z` links still open in both modes. Existing `#project=v1z…` and `#project=v1j…` links open as demos. Invalid links leave the local draft intact.

The implementation uses the same codec and project validation in the app, public module and browser API. Add tests for contract changes and update the schema and instructions together.

## Workspace and recording controls

These operations use the visible interface. They are separate from the project JSON and the browser API.

| Area            | How to use it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Local journeys  | **New journey** opens an empty editor. Set **Journey title** independently of the phone contact name. **My journeys** lists saved drafts and offers copy link, rename and delete. A received link becomes a separate local draft when edited. **Restore from link** reloads its original snapshot.                                                                                                                              |
| Code and Editor | Resize, collapse or reopen **Code**, **Editor** and **Preview**. Use **Copy JSON** for the displayed code. **Validate** checks the draft and **Apply** changes the active journey. Reorder steps by drag or keyboard, and open the action menu to duplicate or remove a step.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Phone preview   | Select a step to inspect it or open **View conversation** for a static overview. Use **Start manually**, **Play automatically**, **Pause playback**, **Resume playback** and **Reset preview**. The 0.5× to 3× pace changes simulated reading, typing and clicks while business delays keep their configured values. Preview links can show a one-time hint pointing to automatic playback.                                     |
| Appearance      | Flags set the interface language without translating the journey. The theme switch changes the workspace and phone, including Flow screens. The seasonal snow control affects the page outside the phone. The preview background is decorative and stays outside the capture.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Phone video     | Select **Record phone** and choose manual or automatic playback. For transparent corners, select **Transparent corners (WebM)** before starting. The clip is 720 × 1440, silent and generated locally. The standard format is MP4 when available, with WebM as fallback. Automatic recording holds the result after completion before finalizing. The destination app must preserve WebM alpha to show the transparent corners. |
| Phone GIF       | Select **Download GIF** in the recording result to convert the existing clip locally to a looping 360 × 720 animation. The GIF preserves transparent corners if the clip was recorded with that option.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

During a recording, `loadProject`, `play`, `stop` and `reset` reject actions that could interrupt capture. Queries, validation and link generation remain available. Use the recording controls to finish or cancel. Links carry the project configuration and language. Local titles, unapplied drafts, preferences, playback history and recordings are separate. See the [user guide](docs/user-guide.md) and [recording reference](docs/recording.md).

## Message body formatting

Use `*bold*`, `_italic_` and `~strikethrough~` in step `text`. Combinations such as `*_text_*` are supported. Preserve the markers in JSON. The phone renders formatting only in message bodies. Button labels and Flow definitions keep their own rules.

## Typed message buttons

For `interactive.kind: "buttons"`, set optional `context` to `"interactive"` (default) or `"template"`. Each button has `id`, `title` and optional `type`: `"quick_reply"` (default), `"url"` with `url`, `"phone_number"` with `phoneNumber`, `"copy_code"` with `code`, or `"voice_call"` with optional integer `ttlMinutes`. See [message rules](docs/messages.md#button-types-and-contexts) before combining types. In mixed templates, `autoReplyId` must target a quick reply; action-only messages may target an action. Action buttons open a phone-contained simulation, not an external site/call/clipboard operation. UI selects are labeled `Message context` and `Button type`; URL, phone, code and TTL fields appear for the chosen type. More than three template buttons use `See all options`.

## Simulated commerce

Add a top-level `catalog` array with up to 200 products. Each product has a unique `sku`, a `name`, a `description` and a positive integer `priceCents` in BRL. Product images are generated from the name. The **Product catalog** editor manages these products. Each commerce step uses `commerce` in place of `interactive`, `media` and `voiceDurationSeconds`.

- A business step uses `{ "kind": "product", "sku": "TV-01" }` for a single product or `{ "kind": "showcase", "sections": [{ "title": "Electronics", "skus": ["TV-01"] }] }` for a grouped offer. A showcase supports up to 10 sections and 30 distinct products.
- A user step uses `{ "kind": "cart", "offerId": "offer" }` to wait for the customer to send a cart from a preceding offer. Set `autoItems` to an array of `{ "sku": "TV-01", "quantity": 2 }` records to configure the automatic cart. Omit the array to select one unit of the first product. Quantities range from 1 to 99. In the showcase editor, **Automatic cart** edits the linked cart or offers to add a **Send cart** step.
- A business step uses `{ "kind": "pix", "amount": { "cartId": "cart" } }` for a simulated Pix charge based on a preceding cart. Use `{ "cents": 249900 }` as the amount for a standalone fixed charge. The phone simulates copying the key and briefly shows **Pix key copied**. The journey advances on that tap while the payment stays pending.
- In `getState().messages`, inspect `commerce.kind === "order"` for the actual order lines and `commerce.kind === "pix"` for the resulting charge in cents. Shared links carry the authored catalog and automatic choices. Each playback starts with an empty cart.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "contact": { "name": "Demo store", "verified": false },
  "catalog": [
    { "sku": "TV-01", "name": "Smart TV", "description": "55-inch display", "priceCents": 249900 },
    { "sku": "SND-01", "name": "Soundbar", "description": "Compact soundbar", "priceCents": 54900 },
    { "sku": "CBL-01", "name": "HDMI cable", "description": "Two meters", "priceCents": 3990 }
  ],
  "steps": [
    {
      "id": "offer",
      "type": "business",
      "text": "What would you like to order?",
      "delay": 1,
      "commerce": {
        "kind": "showcase",
        "sections": [{ "title": "Electronics", "skus": ["TV-01", "SND-01", "CBL-01"] }]
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "cart",
      "type": "user",
      "text": "",
      "delay": 0.4,
      "commerce": {
        "kind": "cart",
        "offerId": "offer",
        "autoItems": [{ "sku": "CBL-01", "quantity": 2 }]
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "payment",
      "type": "business",
      "text": "Here is your simulated Pix charge.",
      "delay": 1,
      "commerce": { "kind": "pix", "amount": { "cartId": "cart" } }
    }
  ]
}
```
